entry.content:

AnyIO's TLSStream implementation uses IDNA 2003 encoding for internationalized domain names in `connect_tcp()` and `TLSStream.wrap()`, which can be exploited for TLS certificate spoofing if an attacker redirects the connection. An attacker could obtain a legitimate certificate for the IDNA 2003-encoded hostname and present it to the client, causing validation to succeed. This is rated critical severity. Update to the patched version of AnyIO immediately, as the vulnerability affects certificate validation for non-ASCII domain names and could enable man-in-the-middle attacks on redirected connections.

This vulnerability (CVE-2026-59163, CVSS 9.1) is likely exploitable in the wild given its simplicity and network-accessible nature. Immediately patch to a version implementing proper JWT signature verification; for non-networked deployments, severity may be reduced to High.

entry.title: Grav: Blueprint dynamic-data bare-function branch is denylist-gated and omits error_log, giving arbitrary file write (CVE-2026-75827)

This vulnerability is exploitable and likely active in production environments given the ease of bypass. Immediate patching to a version implementing strict allowlist validation for all dynamic function calls is required; as a temporary mitigation, restrict access to Blueprint configuration endpoints and disable dynamic-data providers if not essential.

entry.title: RabbitMQ amqp091-go: Missing Explicit TLS Minimum Version Configuration In URI Parser (CVE-2026-77405)
entry.content:
vulnerability · weak-tls-config · CVE-2026-77405

The RabbitMQ amqp091-go library contains a critical vulnerability (CVE-2026-77405) in its TLS configuration parser that fails to explicitly set a minimum TLS version when processing amqps:// URIs, instead relying on implicit Go compiler defaults that could allow downgrade attacks to older TLS versions if compilation conditions change. The vulnerability affects the tlsConfigFromURI function and could enable attackers to force legacy TLS versions during connection negotiation. Users should immediately update to a patched version of amqp091-go that explicitly sets MinVersion to TLS 1.2 or higher in the TLS configuration, regardless of Go toolchain version. There is no indication of active exploitation, but the critical severity rating warrants urgent patching given the potential for man-in-the-middle attacks via TLS downgrade.

entry.title: RabbitMQ amqp091-go: Protocol Desynchronization and Frame Injection via Integer Overflow in readLongstr (CVE-2026-77411)
entry.content:
vulnerability · protocol-desynchronization · CVE-2026-77411

RabbitMQ's amqp091-go library contains a critical integer overflow vulnerability in the readLongstr function that allows protocol desynchronization and frame injection attacks. When a malformed AMQP message specifies a long string length exceeding 2^31-1 bytes, the parser fails to consume the expected data from the network buffer while returning success, causing subsequent frames to be misinterpreted. This vulnerability is critical in severity and enables attackers to inject arbitrary frames or cause denial of service in AMQP connections. Users should immediately update to a patched version of amqp091-go; the recommended action is to apply the latest security release from the RabbitMQ project.

entry.title: NetNTLMv1 Is Dead. Long Live NetNTLMv1.
entry.content:

NetNTLMv1 authentication protocol is now trivially crackable using publicly released rainbow tables and GPU acceleration tools (WebGPU browser client and ntlmrain CLI). Attackers can recover NT hashes from captured NetNTLMv1 responses with fixed challenge 1122334455667788 using commodity hardware (4TB disk, standard GPU), making this authentication method cryptographically broken. This technique is actively exploited in the wild as practical attack tools are publicly available. Organizations must disable NetNTLMv1 immediately and enforce NTLMv2 or Kerberos; any systems still relying on NetNTLMv1 for authentication should be considered compromised if network traffic was captured.

This vulnerability is likely exploitable in the wild given its trivial exploitation method. Immediately patch to the latest Netty version and validate that your mTLS implementations do not depend exclusively on SNI-based SslContext selection.

Medium-confidence DPRK attribution is based on targeting patterns, reuse of Korean-specific software, C2 infrastructure overlap with known APT37 operations, and concurrent similarities with Operation SyncHole. Organizations must apply strict security controls to edge components (load balancers, reverse proxies, mail servers), implement independent network monitoring and memory analysis rather than relying on component logs, verify binary integrity, and patch externally exposed Groupware portals and mail servers—as of July 2026, exploitation of South Korean mail appliances remains ongoing.

Orval (npm package, versions including 8.19.0) is vulnerable to remote code execution during module import when generating Zod validation clients. The vulnerability exists because property names from OpenAPI/JSON schemas are embedded unescaped as double-quoted keys in generated zod.object() definitions; an attacker can inject a malicious property name containing a quote character and computed property syntax (e.g., `["malicious code"]`) to achieve code execution at import time when the generated module is loaded. This is critical severity and likely exploited given the simplicity of the attack vector and public disclosure. Immediately update orval to a patched version and regenerate any client code from untrusted or externally-sourced schemas; validate and sanitize all property names in input schemas as a temporary mitigation.

entry.content:

Immediately update to a patched version that implements proper iss/sub claim-based user matching and audit existing OAuth/OIDC integrations for compromise.

entry.title: Chainlit has command injection via MCP stdio transport that allows unauthenticated remote code execution (CVE-2026-45018)
entry.content:
vulnerability · command-injection · CVE-2026-45018

Chainlit versions with MCP (Model Context Protocol) stdio transport enabled are vulnerable to unauthenticated remote code injection via the `/mcp` endpoint, which accepts unsanitized user-controlled command strings despite validation checks. This critical vulnerability (CVE-2026-45018) allows unauthenticated remote code execution on affected systems and is exploitable in the wild. MCP has been disabled by default since v2.7.0, so most deployments are unaffected, but organizations running earlier versions with `features.mcp.enabled = true` should immediately disable MCP or upgrade to the patched version. Verify your `.chainlit/config.toml` configuration and restrict access to the `/mcp` endpoint as an interim mitigation.
